Subject: Increased inference costs due to prefetch postponement — request for transitional credit

Hi Naomi,

Quick note to flag an operational cost hit we're seeing after Acme pushed our prefetch integration out of the S2 release. Without prefix prefetching we are paying ~35% more per-hour for peak inference (lots of short chat sessions). Our finance team asked whether Redwood can provide a one-time transitional credit while we wait for the prefetch rollout (now scheduled for mid-May).

We attached a short telemetry summary that compares token counts and cost delta for the last three weeks. We're happy to accept a structured credit (one-time credit tied to the next invoice + a temporary per-token rate cap for 30 days) if that helps shorten approval cycles.

Can you advise what the standard approach is for situations where a product timing gap materially impacts customer economics? We have an active commitment (DEAL-ACME-4819) and would like to avoid churn.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Integrations, Acme Corp

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 26 Apr 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Increased inference costs due to prefetch postponement — request for transitional credit

Naomi — quick product update: we delayed the global prefetch rollout to stabilize a KV-cache edge case seen in multi-tenant configs. For Acme's usage profile (high short-session fanout), prefetch will reduce issued tokens by ~30-40% once applied.

Options and timeline: 
- Fast lane patch (projected): targeted prefetch for Acme's model variant by 14 May (2 weeks) if infra team approves a scoped canary.
- Standard rollout: global release in the S2 window (mid-June).

If we take the fast lane it's scoped and may require a small eng investment and more monitoring. That option materially reduces the amount of credit we'd need to offer.

Recommendation: Offer a limited credit tied to a confirmed patch date. If they accept a fast-lane canary with Redwood assistance (1-2 eng checks for first 72 hours), we do: 1) a one-time credit equal to the estimated delta for the delay period (we should align on a formula), 2) a 30-day temporary rate cap to avoid overage surprises. If no fast lane, consider a slightly larger one-time credit and a 14-day rate cap.

I can provide telemetry-based estimates for the credit amount once Marissa gives the target cap or loss tolerance.

-Karthik
Sr. Product Manager, Serving Runtime

Team — drafted options below based on deal size and risk (DEAL-ACME-4819). I used their attached telemetry and our averages to estimate a reasonable commercial fix. I attached a spreadsheet with line-item calculations.

Option A (preferred, conditional on fast-lane patch):
- One-time invoice credit = lesser of (estimated delay cost delta, $60k)
- 30-day per-token rate cap set at their committed rate + 10% for the period
- Acceptance window: customer signs off within 3 business days.
- Governance: requires Director-level approval for credits > $25k; exec sign-off if > $50k.

Option B (no fast lane):
- One-time credit = lesser of (estimated delay cost delta, $95k)
- 14-day rate cap at committed rate + 15%
- Governance: exec approval required.

Ask: Naomi/Monica, would you route Option A to executive sign-off if the fast-lane patch is committed before 14 May? If yes, I can prepare the redlined contract amendment and invoice credit memo.

Marissa
Account Executive, Strategic Sales

Attachment: proposed_credit_summary.xlsx
